- [S2] In simple cases with few objects (e.g., two objects with same intensity/size), using the second derivative field $f''(x)$ as input to $O_{std}$ fails because boundaries are highlighted while interiors become near-zero, causing identical $O_{std}$ values for distinct objects.

The claim is explicitly stated in the notes for Source [S2] and is corroborated by the text in the passages. The passages explain that for simple cases with few objects (e.g., two objects with same intensity/size), using the second derivative field $f''(x)$ results in boundaries being highlighted while other parts become close to zero. This leads to very similar (identical) standard deviation of ambient occlusion ($O_{std}$) values for distinct objects, causing the method to fail. The claim accurately reflects this evidence.
